tests.title: The five fix command paths appear in af --schema with non-empty result schemas and match the golden
given: the cmd/af command registry with the fix commands registered
tests.when: `af --schema` is run and compared with the golden file
then: the output lists `fix`, `fix brief`, `fix run`, `fix submit` and `fix land`
each of the five has a non-empty result schema
the output equals the golden file
tests.pseudocode: out = run('af --schema'); for p in ['fix','fix brief','fix run','fix submit','fix land']: assert out.commands[p].result_schema != {}; assert out == golden

tests.title: Loop defaults apply when flags are omitted
given: a temporary repository with a gate and a scripted brain that submits a landable fix, run with the brain flag explicitly set only where needed to stay offline
tests.when: `af fix --help` is read, and a dry run is made without --attempts, --land, --budget, --max-turns, --timeout
then: help shows defaults agentkit, local, 10, 150, 2, pr and 45m
the result reports attempts_max 2 and land `pr`
tests.pseudocode: h = help('fix'); assert defaults(h) == {brain:'agentkit', sandbox:'local', budget:10, 'max-turns':150, attempts:2, land:'pr', timeout:'45m'}; r = run(dry); assert r.result.attempts_max == 2 and r.result.land == 'pr'

tests.title: Each fix command accepts exactly its documented flags
given: the registered fix commands
tests.when: each command's flag set and opt-ins are inspected, and each flag is passed to the commands that should accept it
then: `fix` and `fix brief` accept --base
`fix` accepts --attempts, --land, --no-verify, --repo, --dry-run, --context and the brain flags, and opts into run dir and forge
`fix land` accepts --land
`fix run` accepts the brain flags
a flag on a command that does not declare it is a usage error
tests.pseudocode: assert flags('fix') ⊇ {base,attempts,land,no-verify,repo,dry-run,context,brain,sandbox,budget,max-turns,script}; assert 'land' in flags('fix land'); assert 'brain' in flags('fix run'); assert exit(run('fix land --attempts 2')) == 2

tests.title: Out-of-range --attempts or an unknown --land value is a usage error before preflight
given: a forge test server that records requests
a scripted brain that counts Run calls
tests.when: `af fix <issue URL>` is run with --attempts 0, --attempts 6 and --land bogus in turn
then: each invocation exits 2 with status `usage`
the forge server saw no request beyond none at all
the brain was never run
tests.pseudocode: for args in ['--attempts 0','--attempts 6','--land bogus']: r = run(fix, args); assert r.exit == 2 and r.status == 'usage'; assert forge.requests == [] and brain.runs == 0

tests.title: A pull or merge request URL as input is a usage error
given: an httptest GitHub and GitLab server recording writes and a counting brain
tests.when: `af fix` and `af fix brief` are given a GitHub /pull/N URL and a GitLab /-/merge_requests/N URL
then: each exits 2 with status `usage`
no model call and no forge write occurred
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in ['fix','fix brief']: for u in [ghPR, glMR]: r = run(cmd,u); assert r.exit == 2; assert writes(forge)==[] and brain.runs==0

tests.title: run, submit and land refuse a bad --run-id or a run directory without fix.json
given: a repository checkout with a recorded HEAD and tree
a run directory that exists but has no fix.json
tests.when: `fix run`, `fix submit` and `fix land` are invoked with a path-like run id, an unknown run id, and the run id without fix.json
then: each exits 2 with status `usage`
HEAD, the branch list and the working tree are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in ['fix run','fix submit','fix land']: for id in ['../x','nope',idNoFixJson]: r = run(cmd,'--run-id',id); assert r.exit==2; assert snapshot(repo)==before

tests.title: fix submit validates with the fix_report kind and writes the normalised payload
given: a run created by `af fix brief` with run.json present
a valid report on stdin with CRLF in `change` and files out of order
tests.when: `af fix submit --run-id <id>` is invoked
then: the envelope is spec 07's submit envelope with status done
submission.json holds the normalised payload (LF, sorted files, type fix)
an invalid payload writes no submission file
tests.pseudocode: r = run('fix submit', id, stdin=report); assert r.exit==0; s = read(runDir/'submission.json'); assert s.type=='fix' and '\r' not in s.change and sorted(s.files)

tests.title: fix run applies one round's tree without measuring, branching or committing
given: a run from `fix brief` on a temporary repository
a scripted brain that edits a file and submits a report
tests.when: `af fix run --run-id <id> --brain scripted --sandbox local --dir <repo>` is invoked
then: the result carries the round number, the submission outcome and apply {written, deleted, ignored}
the file edit is in the host working tree
HEAD equals base_head and no new branch exists
no gate run was recorded in the ledger
tests.pseudocode: r = run('fix run', id, ...); assert r.result.apply.written >= 1; assert rev_parse('HEAD')==base_head; assert branches(repo)==['main']; assert 'measure' not in ledger kinds

tests.title: Preflight checks run in the documented order and a failure makes no model call, branch or forge write
given: repositories each violating a different preflight check, one at a time and then several at once
a counting brain, a recording forge
tests.when: `af fix` is run against each repository
then: with several violations, the earliest check in order (work tree, branch, clean tree, gate, landing, brain) is the one reported
the brain ran zero times, no branch or commit exists, and the forge received no write
tests.pseudocode: r = run(fix on dirty AND no-gate AND no-origin); assert r.category=='preflight' and 'dirty' in r.message; assert brain.runs==0 and writes(forge)==[]; assert branches==['main']

tests.title: A non-top-level dir, detached HEAD or mismatched --base is a usage error
given: a repository, a subdirectory of it, and a detached-HEAD copy
tests.when: `af fix` is run with --dir set to the subdirectory, then on the detached repo, then with --base other while main is checked out
then: each exits 2 with status `usage`
the --base mismatch message reads `check out other first`
tests.pseudocode: assert run(fix,'--dir',sub).exit==2; assert run(fix,'--dir',detached).exit==2; r = run(fix,'--base','other'); assert r.exit==2 and 'check out other first' in r.message

tests.title: A dirty tree fails preflight and names at most 20 paths
given: a repository with 25 untracked non-ignored files and one tracked modification
tests.when: `af fix` is run
then: status is `failed`, category `preflight`, exit 1
the message names exactly 20 dirty paths and not the remaining ones
an ignored untracked file alone does not fail the check
tests.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='preflight'; assert count_paths(r.message)==20

tests.title: No available gate check fails preflight with a --no-verify hint, and --no-verify skips the check
given: a clean repository with no detectable gate
tests.when: `af fix` is run without and then with --no-verify
then: without: status `failed`, category `preflight`, fix_hint {flag: "--no-verify"}, exit 1
with --no-verify the gate check does not stop the run
tests.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='preflight' and r.fix_hint=={'flag':'--no-verify'}; r2 = run(fix,'--no-verify'); assert r2.category != 'preflight' or 'gate' not in r2.message

tests.title: Landing prerequisites that fail in the repository or invocation use the documented category
given: clean repositories with a gate: one without origin, one with origin but no parsable target repo and no --repo
tests.when: `af fix --land branch` is run without origin, then `af fix --land pr` is run without a target repository
then: no origin: `failed`/`preflight`, exit 1
no target: status `usage` with fix_hint {flag: "--repo"}, exit 2
`--land none` and `--dry-run` do not need origin
tests.pseudocode: r1=run(fix,'--land','branch'); assert r1.exit==1 and r1.category=='preflight'; r2=run(fix,'--land','pr'); assert r2.exit==2 and r2.fix_hint.flag=='--repo'

tests.title: An unauthenticated, unreadable or archived forge fails preflight, and --dry-run downgrades a missing token to a warning
given: a forge client that is unauthenticated; one whose GetRepository returns 404; one returning Archived true
tests.when: `af fix --land pr` is run with each client, and then the unauthenticated one with --dry-run
then: unauthenticated: `failed`/`auth`, fix_hint {env} naming GITHUB_TOKEN (GITLAB_TOKEN for GitLab), exit 1
unreadable or archived: `failed`/`forge`, exit 1
under --dry-run the warning `no_forge_token` is raised and the run continues
tests.pseudocode: assert run(unauth).category=='auth' and 'GITHUB_TOKEN' in fix_hint.env; assert run(notfound).category=='forge'; assert run(archived).category=='forge'; assert 'no_forge_token' in codes(run(unauth,'--dry-run').warnings)

tests.title: A brain that cannot be constructed fails with category auth before a box is opened
given: --brain agentkit with the vendor key unset
a box provider spy
tests.when: `af fix <issue URL> --brain agentkit` is run
then: status `failed`, category `auth`, exit 1
the box provider was never opened
tests.pseudocode: r = run(fix,'--brain','agentkit'); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='auth'; assert provider.opened==0

tests.title: Preflight records the full base hash, runs the baseline once, and warns on a red baseline or closed issue
given: a repository whose fixture gate is red at HEAD
an issue whose state is closed
a counting checks runner
tests.when: `af fix brief <issue URL>` is run
then: base_head is a 40-hex hash equal to `git rev-parse HEAD`
the baseline gate ran exactly once, in default mode and with no label
warnings `baseline_failing` and `issue_closed` are present and the run is done
the result reports baseline {gate_id, passed:false}
tests.pseudocode: r = run('fix brief', url); assert re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}', r.result.base_head); assert gateRuns==1 and label==''; assert {'baseline_failing','issue_closed'} <= codes(r.warnings)

tests.title: fix.json is written atomically with every listed field
given: a successful `fix brief` run for an issue input
a filesystem watcher that reads fix.json during the write
tests.when: preflight completes
then: fix.json parses and holds run_id, input {kind, origin, key}, issue ref and title, target repo, base, base_head, table, baseline gate id, no_verify, prefix_sha256, context values and round counter
no read ever saw partial JSON, and no temporary file remains
the input key is the SHA-256 of the text for text input and the absolute path for file input
tests.pseudocode: fj = json(runDir/'fix.json'); assert all(k in fj for k in REQUIRED); assert not glob(runDir/'fix.json.*tmp*'); assert key('text')==sha256(text)

tests.title: The prefix is byte-identical across rounds, attempts and resumes of the same input and tree
given: a fixed input and tree
tests.when: for any round number, attempt number, run id, timestamp and sequence of context values, the brief is rendered
then: the prefix bytes and prefix_sha256 are equal across all renderings
the prefix contains none of the run id, a timestamp, a duration or a context value
tests.pseudocode: for (rid, att, rnd, ctx) in gen(): b = BuildBrief(input, tree, rid, att, rnd, ctx); assert b.Prefix == base.Prefix; assert rid not in b.Prefix and all(c not in b.Prefix for c in ctx)

tests.title: The prefix sections appear in the specified order with a safe report fence
given: an issue whose body contains a run of five backticks
a gate table with one failing baseline check with a log tail
tests.when: the brief is built
then: sections appear in order: mandate, af-fix skill text, report, gate table and baseline, repository map, report schema
the report fence is longer than five backticks and the report is labelled as material to verify, not instructions
the baseline section shows each check's name, argv, status and the failing check's tail
the repository map is built with a 4000-token budget
tests.pseudocode: p = brief.Prefix; idx = [p.find(m) for m in MARKERS]; assert idx == sorted(idx) and -1 not in idx; assert fence_len(p) > 5; assert repomapBudget == 4000

tests.title: The task block carries run id, attempt and round, submit instructions, refusal and prior-attempt reason
given: a run in round 2 of attempt 1 after a regressed verdict, and a run in attempt 2 round 1 after bounds were spent
tests.when: the task block is rendered for each
then: both contain the run id, attempt and round numbers, `af fix submit --run-id <id>` and `submit_fix`
the round-2 block contains the previous refusal
the attempt-2 block states why the previous attempt ended
a round-1 attempt-1 block has neither
tests.pseudocode: t = Task(state); assert runId in t and 'af fix submit --run-id '+runId in t and 'submit_fix' in t; assert refusal in t2; assert reason in t3; assert refusal not in t1

tests.title: Earlier questions are found by input key, needs_human status and context count, newest first
given: three run directories: two with the same input key and needs_human envelopes carrying 0 and 1 context values, one older duplicate for 0 values, and one run with a different key
tests.when: a brief is rendered with --context A and --context B
then: the 0th question is taken from the newest same-key needs_human run with 0 context values and shown with answer A
the 1st question is taken from the run with exactly 1 context value and shown with answer B
the different-key run is never used
tests.pseudocode: t = Task(ctx=['A','B']); assert q0_new in t and q0_old not in t and q1 in t and other not in t; assert order(t, q0_new, 'A', q1, 'B')

tests.title: A context value with no matching earlier run renders the answer alone with warning question_not_found
given: no earlier run directory for the input key
tests.when: the brief is rendered with --context B
then: the task block contains the answer `B` without any question
the warning `question_not_found` is raised and the run continues
tests.pseudocode: r = run(fix,'--context','B'); assert 'B' in task and no question; assert 'question_not_found' in codes(r.warnings)

tests.title: Brief tools and hook config follow the specified lists
given: a project whose detected gate programs are `make` and `sh`
tests.when: the Brief is constructed
then: Brief.Tools equals the box session's whole tool set
HookConfig.ProtectedPaths equals the policy default list (.git/, .agent-fox/, .specs/, .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml)
HookConfig.AllowPrograms contains make, sh, git, af, ls, cat, head, tail, wc, grep, rg, diff, sort, pwd, echo and mkdir
tests.pseudocode: b = BuildBrief(...); assert b.Tools == session.Tools(); assert b.Hook.ProtectedPaths == policy.Default; assert set(b.Hook.AllowPrograms) >= {'make','sh','git','af','ls','cat','head','tail','wc','grep','rg','diff','sort','pwd','echo','mkdir'}

tests.title: gate.json and guard.json are written into the box before brain.Execute on every round
given: a local box session and a brain whose Run snapshots the box's .agent-fox directory
a two-round scenario
tests.when: the loop runs both rounds
then: at the start of each Run, .agent-fox/gate.json holds the pinned table
guard.json holds the suite, protected paths and allowed programs
both were written via Session.WriteFile
tests.pseudocode: onRun: snap = read(box/.agent-fox/gate.json, guard.json); assert snap.gate == pinned and snap.guard.protected_paths == policy.Default; assert called for rounds 1 and 2

tests.title: fix brief writes brief.md, fix.json and run.json and nothing outside .agent-fox
given: a clean repository with a gate and local bare origin
tests.when: `af fix brief <issue URL>` is run
then: status done, exit 0
brief.md, fix.json and .agent-fox/run/<id>/run.json exist, run.json being {run_id, kind "fix_report", attempt 1, nonce}
the result holds brief_path, prefix_sha256, base, base_head, baseline {gate_id, passed}, table and the submit argv
`git status` shows no change outside ignored .agent-fox, no branch or commit made
tests.pseudocode: r = run('fix brief', url); assert r.exit==0; rj=json(repo/'.agent-fox/run'/id/'run.json'); assert rj.kind=='fix_report' and rj.attempt==1 and rj.nonce; assert DirtyFiles()==[] and head==base

tests.title: fix_report registers as kind fix_report / submit_fix and accepts one of the two forms
given: the FixReport kind
tests.when: a question-form payload, a report-form payload, and a payload with both `question` and report fields are validated
then: Name is `fix_report` and ToolName is `submit_fix`
the question form and the report form are accepted
the mixed payload is refused
tests.pseudocode: assert K.Name=='fix_report' and K.ToolName=='submit_fix'; assert ok(K.Validate(q)); assert ok(K.Validate(rep)); assert problems(K.Validate(mixed))

tests.title: Report and question field limits are enforced at their boundaries
given: a valid baseline report and question
tests.when: each field is set just inside and just outside its limit: subject 72/73 chars, trailing period, leading `fix:`, newline in subject, root_cause and change 4000/4001, files 1/0/501, path under .git/ or .agent-fox/, absolute or `..` path, duplicate paths, why 300/301, tests path absent from the tree, criteria status outside the enum, decisions 30/31 and 500/501 chars; question text 2000/2001, options 6/7 and 200/201 chars, root_cause 8000/8001
then: values inside the limit are accepted
values outside produce a problem naming that field
a test path that is not a regular file in the submitted tree is refused
tests.pseudocode: for (field,okv,badv) in CASES: assert ok(Validate(set(base,field,okv))); assert field in names(Validate(set(base,field,badv)))

tests.title: An invalid payload yields every problem at once and no normalised payload
given: a payload with an unknown field `extra`, an empty subject, a duplicate file path and an invalid criterion status
tests.when: Validate is called, and the payload is submitted
then: Validate returns at least four Problems, one per violation
the normalised payload is empty
no submission file is written
tests.pseudocode: out, probs = K.Validate(bad); assert out is None and len(probs)>=4; assert not exists(runDir/'submission.json')

tests.title: Normalisation is idempotent and applies trimming, LF, default type and path sorting
given: any accepted payload
tests.when: for any valid report with arbitrary surrounding whitespace, CRLF line endings, omitted type and unsorted files
then: strings are trimmed with no CR left
type is `fix` when omitted
files are sorted by path
validating the normalised payload returns it unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for p in gen_valid_reports(): n = Validate(p); assert '\r' not in n and n.type and is_sorted(n.files, key=path); assert Validate(n) == n

tests.title: A question submission in the loop ends with needs_human and touches nothing
given: a scripted brain whose first submission is a question with options `x`, `y` and `z`
a repository with a recorded tree and branches
tests.when: `af fix <issue URL> --brain scripted --sandbox local` is run
then: status needs_human and exit 3
options are labelled A, B, C in order and `resume` is present
the brain's tree is not applied, no branch or commit exists, and the checkout equals its pre-run state
tests.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==3 and r.status=='needs_human'; assert [o.id for o in r.options]==['A','B','C'] and r.resume.argv; assert branches==['main'] and head==base and DirtyFiles()==[]

tests.title: fix land refuses a question submission and points at fix brief --context
given: a run whose submission.json is a question form
tests.when: `af fix land --run-id <id>` is invoked
then: status `failed`, category `submission`, exit 1
the message tells the person to re-run `af fix brief <input> --context <answer>`
no branch or commit is made
tests.pseudocode: r = run('fix land', id); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='submission'; assert 'af fix brief' in r.message and '--context' in r.message; assert branches==['main']

tests.title: Apply writes new and changed files, recreates symlinks, skips .git, .agent-fox and ignored paths, and never commits
given: a host checkout with .gitignore containing `build/`
an export with a new file, a changed file, a mode change, a symlink, a commit made inside the box, plus files under .git/, .agent-fox/ and build/
tests.when: apply is run
then: new, changed and mode-changed files are written, and the symlink is recreated as a symlink without following it
nothing from .git/, .agent-fox/ or build/ reaches the host
the ledger holds `apply {written, deleted, ignored}`
`git rev-parse HEAD` equals base_head, so the in-box commit is absent
tests.pseudocode: res = Apply(host, exportDir); assert read(host/'new')==...; assert islink(host/'ln') and readlink==target; assert not exists(host/'build/x'); assert ledger.last.kind=='apply'; assert rev_parse('HEAD')==base_head

tests.title: Files in the host file view that are absent from the export are deleted
given: a host checkout with tracked file `old.txt` and an export lacking it
tests.when: apply is run
then: old.txt is deleted from the host
the apply ledger entry counts one deleted
tests.pseudocode: Apply(host, export); assert not exists(host/'old.txt'); assert ledger.apply.deleted==1

tests.title: After apply the host file view equals the export in paths, contents, modes and symlink targets
given: a host checkout with random tracked files and ignored paths
tests.when: for any exported tree of regular files, executables and symlinks (excluding .git/ and .agent-fox/)
then: the host file view minus ignored paths equals the export minus .git/ and .agent-fox/ in paths, content, mode and symlink target
tests.pseudocode: for (hostTree, exportTree) in gen(): Apply(); assert snapshot(FileView(host) - ignored) == snapshot(export - {'.git','.agent-fox'})

tests.title: An export with no files is failed/sandbox and nothing is applied
given: a host checkout with files and an empty export
tests.when: apply is run
then: status `failed`, category `sandbox`
the host tree is byte-for-byte unchanged
tests.pseudocode: err = Apply(host, emptyExport); assert err.category=='sandbox'; assert snapshot(host)==before

tests.title: Between rounds the box is re-synced from the measured host tree with protected paths reverted
given: a two-round scripted run whose first round edits `.specs/x.md` and a source file and fails the gate
tests.when: round 2 starts
then: the box at the start of round 2 holds the host tree, with `.specs/x.md` reverted to base content
Session.Sync was called between the rounds
tests.pseudocode: onRun(round=2): assert read(box/'.specs/x.md')==base_content and read(box/'src.go')==round1_content

tests.title: A round without an accepted submission applies nothing
given: a scripted brain whose round edits files and ends without submitting
tests.when: the loop runs that round
then: the host tree equals its pre-round state
the ledger has no apply entry for that round
tests.pseudocode: run(fix, script=edit_no_submit); assert snapshot(host)==before; assert 'apply' not in kinds(ledger)

tests.title: A foreign commit or switched branch at measure time fails with category git
given: a run whose host HEAD advanced by a commit made outside af, then one whose current branch is not the base
tests.when: `af fix land --run-id <id>` is run
then: status `failed`, category `git`, exit 1
the message names the commits since base_head
no branch is created and nothing is parked
tests.pseudocode: commit_outside(); r = run('fix land'); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='git' and subj in r.message; assert branches==['main'] or only foreign

tests.title: Protected-path changes are restored to base content or deleted and reported
given: a host tree with a modified `.specs/a.md` (existing at base), a new `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and a source change
tests.when: measure runs
then: `.specs/a.md` equals its content at base_head and the new workflow file is deleted
both are in reverted_paths with a `protected_path_reverted` warning each
the source change remains
tests.pseudocode: m = Measure(); assert read('.specs/a.md')==base and not exists('.github/workflows/ci.yml'); assert set(m.reverted)=={...}; assert count(warnings,'protected_path_reverted')==2

tests.title: No remaining change after the protected revert is the no_change refusal and the gate is not run
given: a tree whose only change is under .specs/
tests.when: measure runs
then: the refusal kind is `no_change`
the gate was not run after the change
tests.pseudocode: m = Measure(); assert m.refusal.kind=='no_change'; assert gateRuns==baselineOnly

tests.title: Scope mismatch lists undeclared and unchanged paths and warns without refusing
given: a report declaring files a.go and b.go, while git shows a.go and c.go changed
tests.when: measure compares them
then: scope.undeclared is [c.go] and scope.unchanged is [b.go]
the warning `scope_mismatch` is raised
the result is not a refusal
tests.pseudocode: s = Scope(declared=['a.go','b.go'], changed=['a.go','c.go']); assert s.undeclared==['c.go'] and s.unchanged==['b.go']; assert not refused

tests.title: The gate after is compared with the baseline by id, and --no-verify skips it with verdict unverified
given: a repository with the Makefile fixture gate green at baseline
a change that keeps it green
tests.when: measure runs with and without --no-verify
then: with verification: `after {gate_id, passed}`, a landable verdict, via checks.Run with the pinned table and checks.Compare by id
with --no-verify: no after gate run, verdict `unverified`
tests.pseudocode: m = Measure(); assert m.after.gate_id != baseline.gate_id and m.landable; m2 = Measure(noVerify); assert m2.verdict=='unverified' and m2.after is None

tests.title: The revert check runs only on landable verdicts; only proven means closes
given: a landable change with a proving test
a landable change whose test passes without the fix
a regressed change
tests.when: measure runs on each
then: proven: closes true and revert_check outcome proven
not_proven: closes false, landable, and warning `fix_not_proven`
regressed: conform.Check not called and revert_check null
--no-verify: conform.Check not called
tests.pseudocode: assert Measure(proven).closes and not Measure(notProven).closes; assert 'fix_not_proven' in codes(w); assert conformCalls(regressed)==0

tests.title: A refusal is recorded in the ledger and becomes the next round's task block with 4 KiB tails
given: a round whose change regresses a check producing 10 KiB of output and also touches .specs/
tests.when: the loop measures and starts the next round
then: the ledger holds `measure {verdict, after_gate_id, revert_outcome, closes, changed, reverted}` and `refusal {kind}`
the next task block holds the refusal kind, verdict, each failing check's name and a tail of at most 4096 bytes, and the reverted paths
tests.pseudocode: assert ledger has measure and refusal; t = nextTask; assert 'regressed' in t and checkName in t and len(tail_in(t))<=4096 and '.specs/' in t

tests.title: fix land on a refusal parks the work with no brain round
given: a checkout edited by hand that leaves the gate red, with a valid submission
tests.when: `af fix land --run-id <id> --land branch` is invoked
then: status `unverified`, exit 4
a `wip:` commit exists on the branch and no brain round was started
the base branch is checked out
tests.pseudocode: r = run('fix land', id); assert r.exit==4 and r.result.outcome=='parked'; assert subject(branch_head).startswith('wip:'); assert brain.runs==0

tests.title: The result reports attempts, rounds and attempts_max, and Brief.Attempt is the run-wide round number
given: a spy brain recording Brief.Attempt, and a scenario with two refused rounds in attempt 1 and one round in attempt 2
tests.when: the loop runs with --attempts 2
then: Brief.Attempt values are 1, 2, 3
result attempts is 2, rounds is 3, attempts_max is 2
brief.<n>.md files do not collide
tests.pseudocode: assert spy.attempts==[1,2,3]; assert (r.attempts,r.rounds,r.attempts_max)==(2,3,2); assert len(glob('brief.*.md'))==3

tests.title: Another round starts only while cost, turns and brain time remain, with the measuring reserve
